metadata.title: OpenTUI visual P0 theme parity leaf slice

work.objective: Make the OpenTUI theme leaf derive its complete palette and syntax state from themeManager's active Ink theme, apply both mutable color and syntax state atomically, expose border/symbol parity, and keep Auto synchronized with terminal light/dark changes without touching dialogs or the renderer backend.
constraints: Use repository-relative paths for every read, search, edit and command.

Only modify the six allowlisted theme implementation/test files; do not change backend, dialogs, Ink components, the canonical themes/theme-manager modules, dependencies, lockfiles, Marshal state, Git history, publication, network state or subagents.
Treat themeManager.getActiveTheme() and its resolved Theme semanticColors/hljs map as the sole color source. Do not retain or introduce a second hard-coded OpenTUI dark/light palette.

Define and test applyThemeDefinition so one call synchronizes the exported mutable C palette and exported SYNTAX value from the same OpenTuiThemeDefinition; callers must not be able to observe a palette from one theme with syntax from another after the call returns.

Extend OpenTUI palette semantics to include at least default border, focused border and UI symbol values, mapped exactly from Theme.semanticColors.border.default, Theme.semanticColors.border.focused and Theme.semanticColors.ui.symbol. Preserve empty strings for NoColor/terminal-default semantics.

Keep syntax mapping derived from Theme.getInkColor and preserve fixed markdown emphasis/strong semantics. Avoid import-cycle or eager-native-initialization regressions; tests must be able to mock @opentui/core without loading native FFI.

Auto mode must choose Qwen Light/Qwen Dark through themeManager and re-apply the manager's active theme on initial terminal detection and subsequent theme_mode events. Explicitly selected non-Auto themes must not be overwritten by terminal events. Subscription cleanup must remain exact and idempotent.
Preserve COLORFGBG -> renderer OSC 10/11 -> macOS appearance -> dark fallback order and the existing 200 ms probe timeout.

Add focused tests for active-theme single-source behavior, C/SYNTAX synchronization, border/symbol/NoColor semantics, Auto initial application, live light/dark switching, explicit-theme stability and unsubscribe behavior.
Do not claim screen-level visual parity from this leaf slice; it only establishes canonical theme state for later Header/Composer/Footer consumers.
If an operation is denied by permission policy, do not retry that path; use an allowed equivalent input or report blocked. Do not mutate the Git index.
context: The current packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/theme.ts owns a hard-coded DARK/LIGHT palette and rebuilds SYNTAX independently through applyThemeMode, while theme-parity.ts already derives an OpenTuiThemeDefinition from the Ink ThemeManager. This duplicates theme truth and can leave selected/custom/NoColor themes visually inconsistent.

The canonical Ink source exposes themeManager.getActiveTheme(), Theme.semanticColors (text/background/border/ui/status) and Theme.getInkColor(). OpenTUI must consume those resolved values rather than approximate Qwen colors.

theme-auto.ts already contains terminal detection and theme_mode subscription primitives. This slice should add a small testable Auto coordinator/application path within the allowlisted files; wiring backend/dialog consumers is deliberately deferred.

Expected semantic mapping includes existing text/dim/accent/status/hover keys plus borderDefault <- semantic.border.default, borderFocused <- semantic.border.focused and symbol <- semantic.ui.symbol. NoColor empty values are meaningful and must not be replaced with fallback colors.
The branch already has native Bun runtime gates. Do not introduce module-load behavior that requires OpenTUI native FFI under ordinary Node/Vitest imports.
nonGoals: No Header, Tips, message, Thought, Composer, LoadingIndicator or Footer layout changes
No canonical Ink theme or ThemeManager changes
